utterances.text: Is the Prosecution ready to start its cross-examination? If you want to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Gajic, you'll now be cross-examined by Ms. Hasan. You'll find Ms. Hasan to your right. Ms. Hasan is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: [In English] Good morning. [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just some points of clarification about the unit that you were in. Now, you were a member of the 1st Company of the Jahorina training centre; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you were part of the 2nd Platoon of that company?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: No, the 1st.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Who was your platoon commander?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Goran Markovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And as far as you recall, Mendeljev Djuric was the company commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you recall Mendeljev Djuric going by any nickname?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Mane.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And do I have it right that Dusko Jevic was Mane's superior?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Gajic, when you spoke about the men who were taken across the factory to the white house, across from the factory to the white house, and you mention that you had seen a pile of belongings, now, these men were made to drop those belongings outside the house as they entered; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan. Witness, did you see that personally, that they dropped their belongings there, or is it your conclusion on the basis of that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is my conclusion. I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please always be very clear in what you saw and what you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- concluded.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Gajic. Then who was it that took the personal belongings from these men? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: I suppose it was done by the soldiers and police officers who were present.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. I just would like to take you on this point back to an interview you gave in Belgrade. If you recall, that took place on the 5th of May, 2011, before the High Court in Belgrade. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I testified.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you told the truth?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we take a look at 65 ter 33279, page 45 in the English, page 40 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, I suppose, sir, that you can follow in either the B/C/S or the English, as you wish. In the English, it's about -- starts at the third paragraph, and in the B/C/S it's approximately two-thirds of the way down the page. And you were asked by the deputy prosecutor of the Bosnia and Herzegovina office of the prosecutor: "Apart from the personal belongings from the separated men which you mentioned, did you see any other things being taken from them?" And your answer was: "No, personal belongings were taken, bags." Then you're asked: "Did you see personal documents being taken away from them?" Answer: "Yes, I did. I mean, I learned later that they were taken away, even money was taken away, so that." Question: "Do you know who did that? That is, members of which unit did that? "Well it was done by, partly, for instance, by the army and partly by the guys I was with." Question: "So members of the unit in which you were?" Answer: "Yes." Mr. Gajic, was that -- were those truthful answers that you gave? Do you stand by that testimony?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: The answers are truthful. I did not personally see possessions being taken. It says here in the third paragraph from the bottom I think I learned later that they were taken away, the things. I could see stuff being taken away, but I didn't see when exactly. What I did see was an enormous pile of items in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And in seeing that pile collect in front of the house, it was your conclusion that these belongings were taken from the men by members of the army and by members of your unit. Have I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, on the 13th of July, you depart and you return back to Bjelovac. Were there guards securing the men who were still in the white house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: I suppose there was a military unit that was left behind to guard the people at the white house, but I don't know any more than that. We left the area at around 6.00 p.m. All the people that had been separated were in the white house and just behind it. It is certain that someone was left there to guard them. I don't know who but I think a military formation was left behind. As far as I know, all members of my unit were withdrawn from that area. As far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, after that second day that you were in Potocari, you returned to your base at the school. And am I correct that you are then awoken at around midnight, thereabouts, and you receive a new assignment? Do I have the chronology right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. The unit set out to a new task immediately after midnight. Perhaps between 1.00 and 2.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you are taken -- if you can correct me if I'm wrong on this, but you are taken by buses to a location very near to the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: That is right. At that moment we didn't know where we were going. Later when we arrived, it turned out to be a facility of the agricultural co-operative in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. This part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This part of examination leaves the topics covered by examination-in-chief. I don't think such questions have been asked of the witness. I did not deal with that part of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, do I have to remind you what the limits are for cross-examination? Could you tell me what is in the Rule which says which are the boundaries for cross-examination? Is that exclusively the subject matter touched upon in examination-in-chief or is there more in the Rules?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Rule does envisage this possibility of going beyond. I am aware of that fact. However, these questions have been very specific and that is why I wanted my objection recorded in the transcript before the Prosecutor continues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any issue about specificity in that Rule? What -- could you tell me what questions can be asked in cross-examination apart from what is touched upon in examination-in-chief? There are two other categories.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if you were to examine me, Your Honour, I don't have the Rules before me, but I know that any question that goes beyond examination-in-chief that could compromise the testimony could be put in cross-examination. I have no doubt about that. And that is not in dispute. However, for these specific questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, let me read the Rule which you should have done yourself before you raised this objection. "Cross-examination shall be limited to the subject-matter of the evidence-in-chief and matters affecting the credibility of the witness and, where the witness is able to give evidence relevant for the case for the cross-examining party, to the subject-matter of that case." Your objection makes me believe that you may have ignored the last portion of that Rule, and Ms. Hasan may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note that it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's time for the break. You're right, Ms. Hasan. Witness, we'll take a break of 20 minutes. We'd like to see you back at quarter past 12.00. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll wait for the witness to enter the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You'll recall, Mr. Gajic, that we just left off talking about your deployment on the night -- morning -- early morning hours of the 14th of July. Now, where was it in relation to the Kravica warehouse or the Kravica farming co-operative that you were dropped off with the buses, as far as you remember?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: It was exactly in front of the warehouse in Kravica. That is where we got off the bus. As we were leaving the bus, we were ordered to go in the direction of Konjevic Polje as part of a column. As we were getting off the bus, we could see soldiers holding some people at gunpoint. Since it was dark, we couldn't see what was going on exactly, but there were people in the warehouse itself who were being shot at by the two soldiers we saw there. We continued moving towards Konjevic Polje and then we stopped, and I stopped some 400 to 500 metres away from the warehouse itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The soldiers that you mentioned outside of the Kravica warehouse, which unit, if you know, did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: At the moment as we were getting off the bus, I didn't know. However, later, when we came to replace the soldiers who were on the road, we learned that they belonged to the Sekovici Special Police Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And just briefly if you can tell us what it was that you were tasked to do?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Our task was to secure the road from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And did your task include the capture of Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And did you capture any Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think two or three people surrendered on that part of the road where I was. I didn't capture them. They surrendered themselves because previously a vehicle had gone through calling to the people to surrender.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And these two, I think you said, two --

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Two or three. I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Two or three men that were -- that surrendered and were captured, what -- what did you do with them?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: The task was that those who surrendered themselves be put on the trucks moving along the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road. Those who surrendered were put on those trucks and taken to the warehouse at Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you recall the types of trucks that were carrying these captured Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: They were military trucks, as far as I remember, that used to belong to the SFRY Army. There was a larger truck, i.e., 150, that could hold more people, and there were two 110s or number 7s that could hold fewer. In any case, the three trucks were used to transport the people.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: These men that were transported to the Kravica warehouse, what happened to them, if you know?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: I know they were liquidated.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And what do you mean when you say "they were liquidated"?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And in addition to these men that were sent to the Kravica warehouse and killed there, did you receive any other information about what had happened at the Kravica warehouse prior to your arrival there in the early morning hours of the 14th? And as far -- as best as you can recall, tell us what it is that you learned.

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: I don't remember specifically. There was an incident that we learned about later on, but I do not know any specific details about the incident. It involved members of the Sekovici Special Brigade and the people who were held prisoner there. I don't know any other details. There was some talk that an incident happened, but I don't know any details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, could I just ask clarification on one matter. You said the two or three which surrendered were taken to the Kravica warehouse and they were killed. Now, how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At approximately 10.00 a.m. until 5.00 p.m. on the 14th of July, one could hear occasional bursts of fire from the direction of the warehouse. At first we didn't know what was going on, but later the rumour had it that the people were being killed there in front of the co-operative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore it was your conclusion. What you know is that they were taken there --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and you concluded --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- on the basis of what you heard --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and on the basis of what rumours told you after that, that they had been killed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was my conclusion on that basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I again may urge you. For us it's important to know exactly what you've seen and what you tell us has happened which you have not seen yourself. So part of it you have seen, you have heard some things. "Heard," I mean fire. And then other is rumours. Could you try to always be as precise as possible, especially in that respect. Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I also have one or two questions for clarification. Sir, you mentioned a little earlier that two soldiers were shooting people in the Kravica warehouse as you passed there. Do you remember that part of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Were you able to see more or less how many people were there inside the warehouse who were being shot at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not saying an exact number but an estimate. You're not --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. It was night-time, that is why we couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Then you talked about these trucks that were carrying people to the Kravica later as you walked along. You've mentioned the three that were -- the people who surrendered. Were they the only three in those trucks or were there other people in the trucks who were transported to Kravica at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The people were brought in front of the warehouse in this way: Those Bosniaks who surrendered were put on trucks which went up and down the road from Kravica towards Konjevic Polje. Those who surrendered were put in the trucks. And when a truck was full, after it had done its round, it went back. And the people who had surrendered would then be taken -- were then taken to the agricultural co-operative in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. You say the trucks were full. That was the answer to my question. More or less how many people could each truck carry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 110 cannot hold many people, perhaps six or seven. Of course, some can also stand while others are seated. As for the 150, together, standing and seated, there could be around 25 or 30 people. The 150 is far greater than the other truck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Were you able to note how many times each of these trucks went up and down with the load to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think between eight and ten times. I don't know exactly. But this would just be an estimate of mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Between eight and ten times carrying either 25 or seven people. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it wasn't always full. It wasn't always full.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we take a look at 65 ter 33279, page 31 in the English, and page 28 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Gajic, this again is the examination that was conducted in Belgrade on the 5th of May, 2011, before the High Court there. And just towards the end in the English and about the middle of the page in the B/C/S, you were asked about what had happened to the persons who were transported to the Kravica warehouse who had surrendered, and then you were asked, question: "Did you hear only about them or some others as well?" Answer: "And we also heard that those who had been there previously from Sekovici, they had practically carried out a large number of these executions." Question: "Who did you hear that from?" Answer: "Well, from the guys who went down there." Question: "What does 'guys who went down there' mean?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, may I interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In the text we just had in front of us, now we've moved to the next page, it is slightly different. Can we go back? It says: "From the guys who were there," not "went down there." "Who were there."

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And then the judge said: "What does 'the guys who were there' mean?"

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Answer: "Well, from the guys I was with in the platoon. We were stationed some 400 to 500 metres above. I did not go down there. I was not present. I did not watch the goings-on." Now, what I've read so far, Mr. Gajic, do you stand by those answers you gave?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: I said here that I found out from the guys who were with me in the platoon, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, we're now looking for the second time to this transcript or report about an interview. I'm a bit confused, and perhaps the parties could seek an agreement on that. It was presented as an interview that was given in Belgrade. It was before the High Court in Belgrade. And a little bit further down, it says that questions were asked by the deputy prosecutor of the Bosnia and Herzegovina office of the prosecutor. Now, I can imagine a few situations. That is, that it was a letters rogatory examination by one prosecutor in another jurisdiction, but it's a bit unclear to me -- I don't know whether the parties could seek an agreement on what is exactly the procedural context in which we have to look at this interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I can discuss it with Mr. Stojanovic. It's clear from -- which I didn't put on the screen, which was this was -- these were proceedings pursuant to letters rogatory by the BiH war crimes office and were conducted in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I saw Mr. Stojanovic nodding in the affirmative, so the Chamber then takes it that this is the procedural context in which the witness was at that time interviewed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, now when you learned about what had previously happened at the Kravica warehouse, did you at that point in time hear any story or account of a Serb soldier being killed and a policeman being wounded?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: No, not at that moment. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I invite you again to move a little bit away from the microphone. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And just as a point of clarification, you had learned this not the day of the 13th of July but the day that you were present there on the 14th of July? That you had learned about the executions that --

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was the incident that had occurred. People talked about it a lot. I didn't really put any questions. Before we came it was talked about, that some incident had occurred.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm going to move on now and ask you about the next task that you had received. And after your deployment on the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road, am I correct that you receive an assignment to sweep the terrain?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: That's right. You're right. The morning of the 15th. That's when we set out to sweep the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, I'll get back to when this sweep took place, but do you recall the area in which your -- you and your unit performed this sweep?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: We set out from this road where we were and we went uphill, that is to say, along that part from Kravica towards Konjevic Polje, over those hills between Kravica and Konjevic Polje. That's where the sweep of the terrain took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, if we can look at 65 ter 05235, please. It will momentarily come up in B/C/S as well. There it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So we see here that it's a very urgent order from the special police brigade. You see on the bottom there it's from the commander Goran Saric. And it's addressed to, among others, the Zvornik CJB public security centre, Ljubisa Borovcanin, and it says there Assistant Special Police Brigade Commander Dusko Jevric. Mr. Gajic, do you know of a Dusko Jevric who was the assistant commander?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sorry, is it Dusko Jevric or Dusko Jevic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Jevic, not Jevric. Jevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: All right. Let's look at item 1. And item 1 says: "Urgently form a combat group of battalion strength in the Kravica - Konjevic Polje sector, using the Doboj Special Police Detachment, two/seminar/ companies from Jahorina, and two PJP/special police units/ with the following task: During the course of today, 17 July 1995, conduct a search of the terrain in the Pobudje sector in order to clear finally the right side of the Milici - Drinjaca road and then concentrate forces to search Cerska. "The commander of the Combat Group 2, comprising the units listed in the previous item, is Assistant Special Police Battalion Commander Dusko Jevric."

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Jevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: It goes on at item 3: "Perform the task on 17 July 1995 and prepare to search the terrain on the left side of the road." And very briefly, item 4: "Form Combat Group 1 for the second part of the front." And it goes on to say: "Borovcanin shall appoint the commander and command and control both Combat Groups." Now, you were sent on -- to search the -- to sweep the terrain and Dusko Jevic was your superior there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but as we were sweeping the terrain on the 15th of July, Dusko Jevic was not there. What you showed just now is a completely different event. It has nothing to do with what it was that I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. When you searched the terrain, were you performing this tasks -- task together with members of the army?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was a combined sweep, members of the police and members of the army together.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please be asked again to keep away from the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it might be a solution to have the microphone slightly lower, perhaps, because -- if it would still be clear enough. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the way it stands.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Gajic, you mentioned that this sweep that involved two companies from Jahorina was not the one you were referring to that you say took place on the 15th of July. Have I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. There was one sweep of the terrain when we went on the 15th in combination with the Bratunac Brigade, as far as I can remember, and it was from the area of Kravica towards Konjevic Polje; whereas what you showed, it says here the right bank -- actually, can you return this? It says the right-hand area of the Milici-Drinjaca road. Geographically or substantially this is totally unrelated. On the 17th, 18th, that's when the sweep of the terrain did take place, but I did not participate in that. So these are two different events. On the 15th of July there was one sweep of terrain, and I think that on the 17th and the 18th there was this other sweep, as far as I can remember. So part of our police units had stayed on - had stayed on - in that area there around Bratunac. And then, as far as I know, they went to sweep this terrain. That is what you've shown us just now. But I did not take part in the latter. I took part in the sweep of the terrain on the 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You are aware, aren't you, that your platoon commander, Goran Markovic, was convicted as well as Dusko Jevic, Mendeljev Djuric, for having taken part in the sweep of the terrain that took place on the 17th and 18th of July?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Goran Markovic was set free, as far as I know. As far as I know. He was not accused, as far as I know. And I did take part in these court proceedings. And I don't know -- I don't know these details. Mr. Jevic, Mr. Djuric, they were accused. I don't see that there was anything that was challenged there, as far as I know. I mean ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. You're not aware of Mr. Markovic's conviction. Where were you then on the 17th of July if you weren't ...

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Well, at Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you were there for how many days?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: I think it was two or three days. And then we were given a new assignment.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: We went to the foot of Mount Treskavica. The name of the place is Duga Poljana.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I don't have this on the screen, Your Honours, I don't have the judgement uploaded. And if I may just read an excerpt from that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, any objections to introduce the text of the judgement by --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I have no problem. And I believe this will be clarified once this judgement is shown to the witness, if that is what this is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I think what Ms. Hasan announced is that she cannot show it to the witness at this very point in time. Ms. Hasan, but at least could you be very clear as far as which court, what date, first instance, appeal, whatever --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: -- I'm going to withdraw actually -- withdraw my questioning on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we can agree on that. I was defence counsel in that case and we can agree what the final judgement was in relation to Goran Markovic, so we really shouldn't take up more time with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan withdraws her question in relation to this matter. Then please proceed with your next subject matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, in the sweep that you conducted you encountered some captured Muslim men; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: When we were returning along that road - that is to say, we've completed the sweep of the terrain and we arrived in Konjevic Polje - we went down there, and then we boarded buses and we went back along this road from Konjevic Polje towards Bratunac. I don't know exactly how many kilometres, because I'm not familiar with the terrain at all. I've never been there since and I have never been there before that, that part of Bosnia-Herzegovina. We came across this group of captives, Muslim civilians who were captives. I think it was a military formation that had taken them prisoner, and they were keeping them there on the right-hand side, to the right of the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sir, you're recorded as saying that: "I think it was a military formation that had taken them prisoner ..." Let's just break that down.

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You thought -- what you're saying is you saw members of the Muslim army who were -- no.

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: No, it was civilians. Civilians. People were not in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Those were the -- the men who were captured; am I right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The civilians.

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And who was it who was securing these men, this group of people?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Members of some military unit. I'm not aware of which unit it was. We just stopped there briefly at that location and then we went on towards the base in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And on what side of the road as you're travelling from Konjevic Polje to Bratunac did you see these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: I've already said. On the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any information about what happened to those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I've nothing further, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hasan. Any further questions, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A few questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gajic, if I understood you correctly, during the night of the 14th of July you were deployed 4- or 500 metres away from the Kravica co-operative?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Between your positions and the agricultural co-operative of Kravica, on that day, the 14th, did you notice any members of the Army of Republika Srpska there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric --

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. On that day, did you notice Mr. Mendeljev Djuric nearby anywhere on that day?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell us, when you started sweeping the terrain on the 15th of July, could you please describe for the Court what it was that you found along this route where you were moving? What did you observe, what did you notice?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: When we set out to sweep the terrain, as soon as we started going up there was this forest there and we noticed a few bodies in very bad shape. You couldn't even tell, because they were in such bad shape, whether they were civilians or military. As we went further on, we came across the dead bodies of members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And then at one point when we reached -- I don't know what to call it, a height, we noticed an enormous trace, say, 15 metres wide, where a Muslim column had passed as they were moving, I assume, towards the territory held by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. These traces could be seen for kilometres, and probably many people went that way, I cannot say how many. But it was so wide and it was so clear, so it certainly must have been several kilometres. As you look at it, you could see it for kilometres. We came across equipment that had been thrown -- thrown away, also weapons that had been thrown away. We found all of that en route.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice any people who had committed suicide?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: At one location there were a few bodies hanging. Now, I have to say very clearly to the Judge that it is my conclusion that these people had committed suicide, but that I don't know. But we did see people hanging in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did this sweep of the terrain last?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: The sweep of the terrain lasted during that morning of the 15th of July and ended about 3.00 in the afternoon when we went down to Konjevic Polje, and from there we went back to the base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one clarification. You said that you also found weapons that had been thrown away. Now, apart from whether you were there when they were thrown away, but how many weapons, approximately, and what kind of weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Different types of weapons. We came across hand-held launchers, so-called bazookas. Then individual weapons, that is to say, automatic rifles, pistols. As for the exact number, I cannot say, but there were tens of pieces of weaponry like that strewn about the meadows on both sides of the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask you to tell the Court the following. As for this transfer along the Kravica-Konjevic Polje is concerned and then your stay there and the task that you were given on the 14th and then the task you were given on the 15th concerning the sweep of the terrain, did you get this assignment - you - from police officials or from military officials?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Police officials, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You personally, your unit, did you ever get any concrete orders from any military officers?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, thank you. On behalf of the Defence of General Mladic, we have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have quite a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, can I just take you back to the Kravica warehouse. You remember you mentioned the two policemen who were shooting people in the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: One was shooting and there was this other one who was standing behind him protecting his back, but it was one of them that was doing the shooting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. That's an excellent detail. Do you know what army they belonged to, those two soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You object to a question by --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He said "policeman." I do apologise. I do apologise. I believe that I either received the wrong interpretation or it was misspoken. He said "policeman," whereas what I heard was "soldiers" and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was an inappropriate intervention because the witness used both. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge. I was trying to find the place because I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Soldiers, page 53, line 11: "... we could see soldiers holding some people at gunpoint. Since it was dark, we couldn't see what was going on exactly ..." That's where the soldiers are mentioned, whereas later I think there was another --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but I think earlier he talked about two soldiers shooting --

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Later we learned that they were ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you know, as I ask my question, what army they belonged to, those two who -- one of whom was shooting inside the Kravica or at the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: They were members of the special police brigade from Sekovici. What I said was that as we were leaving our buses, we couldn't see well. At that moment we didn't know what unit they belonged to. Later we found out that the unit in question was a police unit from Sekovici. They were members of the police force.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the Sekovici Special Brigade was a police force. I leave the question now, but I'm going to look for the time -- the place where you talked about two soldiers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further questions, Ms. Hasan, after you have concluded your consultation with Mr. McCloskey? Ms. Hasan, I addressed you, but you may have missed it because you took off your earphones. If you could just look at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I could just have one minute, I'm just seeing if I have one more question -- one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, one minute for one question.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Nothing further, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hasan. If you'd give us one minute for perhaps one question as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, I found the piece of evidence. At page 53, line 10, you said -- no, is it line 10?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right. Sir, on page 53, starting at line 12, you say: "Since it was dark, we couldn't see what was going on exactly, but there were two people in the warehouse itself" -- sorry, I'm sorry. "... who were being shot at by the two soldiers we saw there." Okay. Well, this is how you are recorded and I can see you are shaking your head. But that's how --

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Not correct. I said as follows: As we were leaving the bus, which was stopped right next to the agricultural co-operative at a distance of 7 to 8 metres, as we were leaving the bus I could see silhouettes. One of them belonged to a soldier standing at the very entrance of the warehouse, and we could see that he fired in a particular direction every now and then. There was another soldier standing behind him covering his back, so to say. That's what I said about the two soldiers. They were actually policemen, but I didn't know at the time who or what they were. Later on we learned that they were members of the Sekovici Special Brigade. When we rotated, we took over from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. This is a completely new correction of your testimony. It doesn't tally with what you are recorded as having said. The point at which I'm talking about is the same point where you talked about leaving the bus, and you said: "We were ordered to go in the direction of Konjevic Polje as a part of a column. As we were getting off the bus, we could see soldiers holding some people at gunpoint. Since it was dark, we couldn't see what was going on exactly, but there were people in the warehouse itself who were being shot at by two -- by the two soldiers we saw there." There is no mention of a silhouette and there is no mention of police at this point of your testimony. You are talking about soldiers. So it's a correction of your testimony. Thank you so much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: LJUBODRAG GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Everything being clarified, we have no further questions. Mr. Gajic, I'd like to thank you very much at the conclusion of your testimony for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered the many questions that were put to you, both by the parties and by this Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are close to the point where we would take a break. Would you prefer to take the break now, Mr. Stojanovic, and then start the evidence of the next witness, which is Mr. Poparic, if I am well informed, after the --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour. I would like to seize this opportunity to advise you that Mr. Poparic only just arrived in The Hague today. In that regard, he could only appear as of tomorrow. For the remainder of 40 minutes of work or so today, we have no other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which then means that we would adjourn for the day. Often, of course, we urge you to keep witnesses ready, but in view of the special circumstances where you could, under normal circumstance, expect Mr. Poparic to start his testimony later as he now will do, there is no reason whatsoever to make similar comments as we've made in the past. We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 27th of October, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.
